common_name: Suwannee River Privet (Compact Hybrid Wax-Leaf Ligustrum)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade; Suwannee River privet is a naturally compact hybrid selection that needs far less shearing than full-size wax-leaf ligustrum to hold a tidy mounded form.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade; Suwannee River privet is a naturally compact hybrid selection that needs far less shearing than full-size wax-leaf ligustrum to hold a tidy mounded form. A cross between Ligustrum japonicum and L. lucidum, it carries small, lustrous, deep green evergreen leaves on a dense, rounded, slow-spreading habit that tops out at a fraction of the size of straight wax-leaf privet, reaching only about 3 to 4 feet tall and wide at maturity. Lightly fragrant white flower panicles appear in mid-spring, followed by small dark berries; the plant's naturally dwarf, mounding form makes it useful for low hedges, foundation plantings, and container specimens where a full-size ligustrum would quickly outgrow the space. It tolerates heat, humidity, and light shearing well, and its compact stature reduces the aggressive self-seeding common to larger privet species.
